manifest.name: texra
manifest.description: TeXRA: Your LLM-powered 24/7 LaTeX Research Assistant.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: TeXRA runs AI agents that read workspace files and execute shell commands (LaTeX compilation, bash tools, external MCP tools). Open trusted workspaces only.

commands.title: Apply LaTeX Replacements to Current File
Count Words in Current TeX File
Extract TikZ Figures from Current File
Compile TikZ Figures from Current File

texra.agentOutputs.autoOpenFinal.description: When a workflow run completes, automatically preview the final revised file in a new editor tab. Disable for batch runs when you don't want a tab to steal focus.

texra.experimental.odyssey.enabled.description: Experimental: enable Odyssey, a per-stream autonomous-continuation mode for tool-use agents. When on, an active Odyssey causes the agent to keep working across turns toward a stated objective until it calls odyssey(complete). Off by default; the `odyssey` tool is registered either way but errors out when this flag is off.

texra.inlineCriticism.enabled.description: Experimental: parse \criticize{message}{severity}{confidence} annotations from agent-revised LaTeX files and surface them as VS Code diagnostics (squiggles + Problems panel). Severity 5→Error, 4→Warning, 3→Info, 1–2→Hint. Tool-use agents may also push diagnostics directly via the add_criticism tool.

texra.auth.enableVSCodeGitHub.description: Enable VS Code native GitHub authentication (experimental)

texra.ui.showApiKeyReminders.description: Show API key reminders in the status bar and main view when no API keys are configured

texra.ui.showGettingStartedBanner.description: Show getting started banner with import options when no LaTeX files are found

texra.ui.showLoginBanner.description: Show login banner prompting users to sign in for access to remote agents

texra.ui.showOrchestratorBanner.description: Show orchestrator and session reminder text in the main view

texra.model.compactionThresholdPercent.description: When the conversation reaches this percentage of the model's context limit, TeXRA automatically summarizes earlier messages to free up space. Lower values trigger summarization sooner. Set to 0 to disable.

texra.model.gpt5ReasoningSummary.description: Show the model's reasoning steps alongside its output when using GPT-5 models. Requires an OpenAI account with access to reasoning features.

texra.model.improvedConnectionDomain.description: Domain to use when using improved connection

texra.model.openaiParallelToolCalls.description: Let OpenAI models use multiple tools at the same time for faster results. Disabled by default for more predictable behavior.

texra.model.useBackgroundResponses.description: Keep long-running OpenAI requests alive in the background (polling) instead of timing out after 10 minutes. Applies automatically to GPT models running workflow agents; ignored otherwise. Disable to fall back to synchronous streaming requests.

texra.model.useImprovedConnection.description: Use improved connection for API requests

texra.model.useOpenAIResponsesAPI.description: Use OpenAI's newer Responses API for additional features like built-in tool use. Disable to fall back to the classic Chat Completions API.

texra.files.ignored.directories.description: Directories to ignore when listing files

texra.files.ignored.fileExtensions.description: File extensions to ignore when listing text files

texra.files.ignored.inputDirectories.description: Additional directories to ignore when listing input and edited files

texra.files.ignored.inputFiles.description: Files to ignore when listing input, sample, and edited files

texra.files.ignored.keywords.description: Keywords to ignore when selecting files

texra.files.ignored.mediaDirectories.description: Directories to ignore in the figure path

texra.files.included.contextExtensions.description: File extensions to include when searching for context files

texra.files.included.editedExtensions.description: File extensions to include when searching for edited files

texra.files.included.inputExtensions.description: File extensions to include when searching for input files

texra.files.included.mediaExtensions.description: File extensions to include when searching for media files

texra.maxImageDimension.description: Maximum dimension (width or height) in pixels for images before resizing. Images larger than this will be resized to fit within this dimension while maintaining aspect ratio.

texra.bib.defaultPath.description: Default path to bibliography file (.bib). This is used by bibliography tools when no explicit path is provided. Supports Zotero auto-exported .bib files.

texra.bib.zoteroPort.description: Port number for Zotero integration (default: 23119). Used by both the Connector API and Better BibTeX JSON-RPC.

texra.latex.showLatexindentWarning.description: Show warning when latexindent is not installed

texra.latex.includeWorkspaceInTexinputs.description: Include the workspace root directory in TEXINPUTS when compiling TikZ figures

texra.latex.tikzInputDirectory.description: Directory where to look for extra input files when compiling extracted TikZ figures. Absolute path is required. Sets TEXINPUTS environment variable for TikZ compilation.

texra.latex.tikzTemplate.description: Template used for generating standalone documents when extracting and compiling TikZ figures

texra.latex.customReplacements.description: Custom LaTeX replacements in the format: { 'from': 'to' }. Example: { '\alpha': '\al' }

texra.latex.customReplacementsRegex.description: Custom regex replacements in the format: { 'pattern': 'replacement' }. Use capture groups with $1, $2, etc. Example: { '\\section\{([^}]+)\}': '\section{$1}' }

texra.latex.enabledReplacements.description: List of enabled non-regex LaTeX replacement categories

texra.latex.enabledReplacementsRegex.description: List of enabled regex LaTeX replacement categories

texra.latex.wrapCritiqueInAlign.description: When enabled, bare \critique and \comment commands inside align blocks are wrapped with \intertext.

texra.latexdiff.pictureEnvironments.description: Regular expression pattern for environments to be treated as pictures. These environments will be processed as a unit without internal differencing.

texra.latexdiff.tempFileLocation.description: Where to create temporary files for LaTeX preview and diff operations during tool edit approval.
enumDescriptions: Create temp files in the same directory as the original file. Best for resolving \input{} and relative paths.
Create temp files in .texra-temp directory at workspace root. Keeps source directories clean but may break relative paths.

texra.git.emitPrCiStartedEvents.description: Emit a PR subscription event when GitHub check runs first appear for a new head commit.

texra.git.numberOfCommitsToShow.description: Number of recent commits to show in the commit selection dropdown

texra.audio.soxPath.description: Path to the SoX executable. Overrides automatic detection.

texra.apiKeys.remove.markdownDescription: API keys are now stored securely. [Click here to remove the stored key](command:texra.removeApiKey)

texra.apiKeys.set.markdownDescription: API keys are now stored securely. [Click here to set an API key](command:texra.setApiKey)

texra.debug.saveDebugObjects.description: Save message and response objects to JSON files for debugging purposes

texra.debug.saveInputPrompt.description: Save the final input prompt sent to the model as an XML file for debugging purposes

texra.logger.debugMode.description: Whether to show verbose debug messages in the logger view

texra.toolUse.persistence.enabled.description: Persist tool-use conversations across VS Code restarts

texra.toolUse.persistence.ttlHours.description: Maximum age (in hours) to keep saved tool-use sessions before automatic cleanup

texra.toolUse.requireBashApproval.description: Require user approval before tool-use agents execute bash commands

texra.toolUse.requireEditApproval.description: Require user approval in a diff view before tool-driven edits modify workspace files

texra.model.retry.backoffMs.description: Base backoff delay in milliseconds between retry attempts for model calls

texra.model.retry.maxAttempts.description: Number of automatic retry attempts before surfacing a manual retry option for model calls. Set to 0 for no automatic retries (manual retry button only).

walkthroughs.description: Get TeXRA up and running in a few minutes. Connect your account, pick your field, and run your first paper through the orchestrator.

steps.description:
Start here. TeXRA's setup assistant agent checks your environment, installs any missing LaTeX tools, adds an API key or signs you in, and verifies that you're ready to go. It asks before every command and explains what it's doing.

[Run Setup Assistant Agent](command:texra.runSetupAssistant)

Prefer to do it yourself? The remaining steps walk you through the same checklist manually.
steps.title: Run the setup assistant agent

steps.description:
Not sure where to start? We've bundled a small LaTeX project you can play with.

[Create the sample project](command:texra.createSampleProject)

You'll get a folder with example `.tex` files and a README that explains the layout.
steps.title: Try the sample project

steps.description:
You'll need an API key from a provider like Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google. Just one is enough.

[Set API key](command:texra.setApiKey)

Heads up: chat subscriptions (ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro) don't come with API access. You need a separate key from the provider's developer platform.

**No API key?** No problem -- sign in with the Researcher Access Program in the next step instead.

media.altText: Screenshot of the API key configuration view

steps.title: Add your API key

steps.description:
The **Researcher Access Program** lets you use AI models and remote agents for free -- no API key needed.

[Sign In](command:texra.auth.signIn)

Already set an API key? You can skip this, but signing in still unlocks extra agents you can't get with a key alone.
steps.title: Or just sign in

steps.description:
Open the main view and tell TeXRA what to work on:

- **Input** -- the manuscript you want edited
- **Context** -- bib/style files, reference papers, or any read-only context (optional)
- **Media** -- figures and images (optional)

You really only need an Input file to get going.

[Open the TeXRA main view](command:texra.showMainView)

media.altText: Screenshot of the file selection interface

steps.title: Pick your files

steps.description:
We recommend starting with the **orchestrator**. It reads your paper, figures out what needs work, and hands each task to the right agent automatically.

Just pick **orchestrator** from the agent dropdown. You'll also want to choose a model -- bigger models give better results, smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

If you'd rather do one specific thing (just fix grammar, just draw a diagram), you can pick a single agent instead.

media.altText: Screenshot of the agent and model selection UI

steps.title: Use the orchestrator

steps.description:
We have teams for different disciplines that give the orchestrator the right set of tools for your work:

- **Physicist** -- derivations, numerical experiments, literature, presentations
- **Mathematician** -- proofs, formalization, research
- **Lean Project** -- Lean 4 with theorem search and blueprints

[Open Settings](command:texra.showDashboard) and go to the **Multi-Agent** tab to pick one. You can always tweak it or make your own later.
steps.title: Pick your field

steps.description:
Got figures or TikZ diagrams in your paper? Turn on auto-extraction and TeXRA will pull them out before running.

Flip the **Auto-extract figures** and **Auto-extract TikZ** toggles in the main view. Or run them manually:

[Extract figure paths](command:texra.extractFigurePaths) | [Extract TikZ figures](command:texra.extractTikzFigures)
steps.title: Auto-extract figures (optional)

steps.description:
You're all set. Click Execute and the orchestrator will start working through your paper.

[Execute](command:texra.execute)

It'll propose tasks as it goes -- you'll see each one pop up in the [Progress view](command:texra.showProgressView) where you can approve, tweak, or skip it.

Want it to just run without asking? Turn on **auto-approve** in Settings > Multi-Agent.
steps.title: Hit Execute!

steps.description: Your originals are safe -- TeXRA writes edits to new files. Open them up and use VS Code's diff view to see exactly what changed. Accept what you like, ignore what you don't.

media.altText: Screenshot of the VS Code diff view

steps.title: Check what it did

steps.description:
Happy with the results? Use **Pack** $(archive) to save everything to a `History/` folder. Want to start over? Use **Clean** $(trash) to wipe the generated files.

You'll find both in the Progress toolbar, or right-click any `.tex` file.

[Clean all outputs](command:texra.cleanOutput) | [Clean build files](command:texra.cleanBuild)

media.altText: Screenshot showing pack and clean buttons in the Progress toolbar

steps.title: Clean up when you're done

walkthroughs.title: Get started with TeXRA
